articles.title: Paige Bueckers joins rare company as Dallas Wings surge toward playoffs
articles.standfirst: The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed
articles.summary: The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed
articles.body:
Paige Bueckers arrived in the WNBA carrying enormous expectations. Less than two full seasons later, she is doing something even more impressive: exceeding them. The Dallas Wings superstar added another chapter to her rapidly growing legacy on Saturday night, leading her team to an 87-82 victory over the Phoenix Mercury while setting a new WNBA scoring milestone that further cemented her place among the league's brightest stars.

Bueckers finished with a game-high 26 points, four rebounds, five assists, three steals, and one block as Dallas secured its sixth consecutive victory. The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed the former UConn standout from a highly touted prospect into one of the most impactful players in professional basketball.

The win also came on a historic night

During the game, Bueckers became the highest-scoring player through the first two seasons of a WNBA career . The league announced the achievement on social media shortly after the milestone was reached.

“History. Made: Paige Bueckers has scored the most points (1,515) by any player through their first two seasons in WNBA history!”

The record is notable not only because of the names Bueckers passed, but because of what those names represent. She moved ahead of Hall of Famer Seimone Augustus, who scored 1,513 points through her first two seasons, and surpassed WNBA legend Cynthia Cooper, one of the greatest scorers the sport has ever seen.

Bueckers has benefited from the WNBA's expanded 44-game schedule that began during her rookie season in 2025. Augustus established her mark in 68 games, while Cooper accumulated her total in just 58 contests. Even with that caveat, the accomplishment underscores a reality that has become impossible to ignore.

Bueckers is one of the most gifted offensive players in the sport

She reached the milestone in 75 career games and still has two regular-season contests remaining. More importantly, she has paired her scoring ability with elite playmaking, defensive activity, and leadership, turning herself into the centerpiece of a Dallas team that appears to be peaking at exactly the right time. The six-game winning streak is evidence of that growth.

After spending much of the season fighting for playoff positioning, the Wings have surged into the postseason conversation with momentum on their side. Dallas currently sits at 26-16 and occupies sixth place in the standings with road games remaining against Phoenix and Seattle before the playoffs begin. Bueckers has been the driving force behind that rise.

What makes her ascent especially intriguing is the company she is beginning to keep. For much of the past several years, conversations about the league's biggest stars have centered around players such as A'ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, and, more recently, Caitlin Clark. Wilson remains one of the most dominant two-way players in basketball, while Clark has become one of the most influential stars the WNBA has ever seen thanks to her scoring, passing, and ability to transform an offense.

The reigning Rookie of the Year has already become a two-time All-Star and a FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup gold medalist . More importantly, she has demonstrated the ability to impact every facet of the game. On Saturday alone, she scored efficiently, facilitated the offense, generated turnovers, and protected the rim. Few guards in the league offer that complete package.

articles.title: Angel Reese makes history as Wendell Carter Jr. celebrates in style
articles.summary: Angel Reese's record-breaking 2026 season reached another historic milestone Saturday night, and Wendell Carter Jr. was there to celebrate it in style. The Atlanta Dream star became the first player in WNBA history to collect 500 rebounds in a single season during Atlanta's 106-81 victory over the Chicago Sky. Reese finished with 23 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two steals, helping the Dream secure their eighth win in their last 10 games and strengthen their position heading into the postseason. And after the game, Carter once again made sure the spotlight stayed on Reese. The NBA big man, who has become one of Reese's most visible supporters, was spotted rocking another custom Angel Reese jersey following her latest historic performance. It was a fitting celebration for a player who continues to rewrite the WNBA record book in just her third professional season.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and the Fever steal the spotlight before disappointing home game
articles.standfirst: Indiana had a tough afternoon against Washington, although Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull still found a way to turn heads before the game.
articles.summary: Indiana had a tough afternoon against Washington, although Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull still found a way to turn heads before the game.
articles.body:
This Sunday, the Indiana Fever faced the Washington Mystics at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in a game that ended with a 93-77 Washington victory. Caitlin Clark led Indiana in scoring with 25 points, along with 5 assists, 2 rebounds and 2 steals. Kelsey Mitchell added 22 points, while Lexie Hull finished with 2 points and 2 rebounds .

For Sophie Cunningham, the afternoon was even tougher. She came off the bench and played seven minutes without recording any points, rebounds or assists.

So, if there was anything the Fever could brag about that afternoon, it had to happen before the game even started. Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull arrived at the arena in completely different looks and managed to turn some heads before tipoff .

Caitlin Clark went with burgundy

Clark arrived at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in a sporty look centered around burgundy.

The player wore Nike sweatpants with a white T-shirt from the same brand . She added a white-and-burgundy fleece jacket on top, while her sneakers followed the same color combination.

Dark sunglasses, her hair worn down and a few accessories completed the look she chose for her arrival at the game.

Sophie Cunningham completely changed things up

Cunningham showed up in a much more dressed-up combination. The player opted for a dark brown polo shirt with a gray-and-white skirt .

She completed the look with heels, a black handbag, dark sunglasses and a necklace, while leaving her hair down.

The result was quite different from Clark's sporty outfit, showing that there was more than one way to arrive at the same game.

Lexie Hull found the middle ground

Hull arrived in a white blouse and dark brown shorts, paired with a belt in a lighter shade of brown .

Open-toe heels, a handbag and dark sunglasses completed the outfit, while she also wore her hair down.

Her look landed somewhere between the previous two: dressier than Clark's sporty outfit, but not quite as dressed up as Cunningham's.

Now the Fever will have to turn their attention to Minnesota

The loss to Washington is already behind them, and the Fever will not have much time to dwell on it. Indiana will be back in action on Tuesday, September 22, once again at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, this time against the Minnesota Lynx .

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s violent screaming match with Stephanie White caught on camera
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark wasn’t holding back. The Fever star had a heated exchange with coach Stephanie White during a frustrating loss to the Mystics.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark wasn’t holding back. The Fever star had a heated exchange with coach Stephanie White during a frustrating loss to the Mystics.
articles.body:
C aitlin Clar k once again became a topic of conversation after an interaction that may shed light on her relationship with her coach. The Indiana Feve r star shared a tense moment with head coach Stephanie White during the first quarter against the Washington Mystics , at a time when the team was already in trouble.

With Washington leading 31-17 and 58.7 seconds left in the opening period, Clark walked toward the defensive end, turned toward the bench, and expressed her frustration directly at White in full view of everyone .

The exchange stood out because it came just days after the coach had publicly praised her star’s leadership, even saying that Clark “sounds like a coach.”

As the first quarter neared its end, Clark waited for play to resume but used the moment to address White on the sideline. The coach listened while the Indiana point guard made her dissatisfaction clear.

The exchange reflected Clark’s competitive personality. She consistently takes on a leadership role on the court and does not hesitate to speak up when she believes corrections are needed.

The Mystics had taken complete control of the game. Washington closed the first quarter ahead 34-19 and went into halftime with a 51-30 lead .

Kiki Iriafen was key with 21 points and 14 rebounds, while Shakira Austin added 20 points and 10 rebounds in the 93-77 victory.

For Indiana, Clark finished with 25 points and five assists, and Kelsey Mitchell scored 22 points , but the team never mounted a comeback. With two games remaining, Washington moved to within one game of the Fever in the race for the fifth seed.
